messages:
Maya (Support): forwarding a customer escalation — ACME reports SSE connections for completions keep 'flapping' (disconnects every ~20-40s) and clients sometimes only get partial token streams. They see reconnects but final tokens are missing. They provided trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d and request id: req-9f8e7d6c. Model: gpt-open-13b, region: us-east-1.

Maya (Support): customer says it happens across our hosted endpoint and their dedicated instance. They attached a pcap and a small app repro. Linking pcap: s3://redwood-support/pcaps/1768001234-acme-sse.pcap (internal).

Dan (Eng): thanks — can you paste the root request headers they used and the exact curl/node repro? want to reproduce locally. Also will need the runtime pod logs (redwood-runtime) around the trace id.

Maya (Support): curl they used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "x-redwood-trace-id: trace-0a1b2c3d" \\n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-open-13b"
```
They said client is a web app behind a corporate proxy.

Lee (SRE): initial checks: look for 502/503/504 from front proxy, or proxy idle timeouts killing long-lived connections. Envoy/nginx defaults often 60s. But you're seeing <60s here (20-40s) so could be intermediate NAT/ALB idle or client TCP stack resetting.

Dan (Eng): pulled runtime logs for trace-0a1b2c3d — here's the snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] trace=trace-0a1b2c3d req=req-9f8e7d6c stream: started, seq=0
[2026-03-10T14:02:29Z] trace=trace-0a1b2c3d stream: wrote chunk, seq=12, bytes=128
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] trace=trace-0a1b2c3d transport: write failed: write tcp 10.2.3.4:443->10.8.7.6:52314: write: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-10T14:02:32Z] trace=trace-0a1b2c3d stream: cleanup, reason=transport_error
```
No 5xx from our front-line LB.

Priya (CSE): customer mentioned their client sees the SSE stream close with HTTP/2 GOAWAY in some cases and on reconnect they request the same conversation id but missing the last tokens. They suspect our runtime closed the connection mid-response.

Dan (Eng): the write error looks like the client/edge closed first (reset by peer). We should get the tcpdump from both client side and our egress. Maya — can you ask ACME for a client-side pcap around 14:02:30? Also confirm whether they're using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 for SSE (we support both but behavior differs).

Maya (Support): ACME uploaded client pcap too: s3://redwood-support/pcaps/1768001234-acme-client.pcap. They say their app is using fetch() with EventSource polyfill over HTTP/1.1.

Lee (SRE): action items for observability:
- correlate x-redwood-trace-id across runtime logs, lb access logs, and envoy metrics.
- enable DEBUG streaming logs for the runtime for that trace (set REDWOOD_STREAM_DEBUG=1 on the POD)
- grab tcpdump on the node: `tcpdump -i eth0 host <client_ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/sse-client.pcap`
- check ALB/NGINX idle timeout / keepalive settings and datadog metric `loadbalancer.connection_idle_time` spikes.

Dan (Eng): quick repro I ran with the same curl produced a flaky disconnect after ~25s when I throttled the network (tc qdisc netem). This smells like intermediate network devices dropping idle-ish TLS streams. Some corporate proxies or mobile carrier NATs drop TLS if there's no bytes for X seconds. We emit tokens intermittently; if token cadence stalls for > idle_timeout they close.

Priya (CSE): customer says they saw periods where model generation paused for 6-8s between token batches, then resumed. That pause might trigger the proxy to drop the connection.

Maya (Support): included runtime metrics at the time:
- model generate latency p50: 120ms, p95: 2.1s (spiky), tokens/sec: 18
- streaming_token_gap_count (tokens gaps >2s): 23 in 10 minutes for that route

Dan (Eng): mitigation suggestions to propose to customer:
- implement client-side heartbeat (SSE comment) to keep connection alive: send `:keepalive\\n\\n` every 10s when no payload.
- on reconnect, use idempotency/conversation state to request resume tokens (we can surface last-ack token index in future but currently client should request re-generation).
- server-side: we can enable a short heartbeat from runtime to client (patch available) and increase upstream idle timeout on the proxy to 120s as safe default.

Lee (SRE): longer-term: add metric `sse.keepalive_sent` and an alert if >5% of streaming requests have >1 reconnection in 5m. Also add trace-level correlation for connection resets with `tcp.reset` events in access logs.

Dan (Eng): repro steps we used:
1) `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 0ms loss 0%`
2) run curl from step above
3) `tc qdisc change dev lo root netem delay 100ms` then observe intermittent token pauses and sometimes connection reset.

Maya (Support): asked ACME to try three quick things: set EventSource heartbeat, switch to HTTP/2 if possible, and provide a short client pcap capture. They agreed to test and report back.

Priya (CSE): ACME tried heartbeat and reported a dramatic drop in disconnects. They saw one reconnect vs ~10 previously in same workload. :tada:

Dan (Eng): we should still harden server defaults. I'll open a small PR to:
- add server-side keepalive comment emit every 10s when idle, behind a feature flag
- add a runtime metric for token gap occurrences
- document recommended client-side heartbeat in support KB
PR: internal link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/543

deploy-bot: build/pipeline #543 succeeded (canary image built: runtime:canary-543).

Lee (SRE): next infra steps: bump nginx/proxy idle timeout to 120s for streaming route in staging, run canary for 24h, watch `streaming.reconnect_rate` and `loadbalancer.connection_drops`.

Maya (Support): filing final support note to ACME: include repro steps, link to pcap, recommended client heartbeat, timeout recommendations, and ETA for server canary (24-48h). I'll follow up after they validate in staging.

Dan (Eng): root cause hypothesis: intermediate network devices/proxies closing idle TLS connections when there are token cadence gaps. Fixes: client heartbeat + server keepalive + proxy timeout bump.

Priya (CSE): thanks team — ACME is happy with the workaround and asked us to keep them in the loop for the canary roll.

Maya (Support): marking as monitored; will close escalation once customer confirms stable for 48h.

Maya (Support): notes for postmortem/ticket:
- trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d
- customer impact: partial outputs/reconnects (ACME web app)
- root cause: likely mid-path NAT/proxy idle timeout + token cadence gaps
- mitigations: client heartbeat doc, server keepalive canary, proxy timeout bump, observability metric add

Maya (Support): tagging eng/sre/product to track PR/infra changes.
